question.text: A person starting from point A on one bank of a river intends to reach point B located on the opposing bank downstream. The straight line joining A to B is inclined at an angle of 45° to the line perpendicular to the banks. The water moves at a uniform speed u parallel to the banks.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Determine the lowest possible speed of the person relative to the water that allows them to reach point B.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the heading angle θ (measured upstream from the line perpendicular to the river bank) at which the person must swim.

conditions: river flows horizontally at constant speed u
line AB is inclined at 45° downstream relative to the line perpendicular to the banks
motion relative to water is uniform
man travels directly along the straight path AB

figure.description: A river of uniform width flows horizontally to the right with velocity u. Point A is situated on the bottom bank, and point B is located on the top bank downstream. A perpendicular dashed line across the river from A makes an angle of 45° with the straight line AB connecting A and B.

solution.approach: The resultant velocity must lie along AB, so the swimmer's velocity relative to water is least when perpendicular to AB; find it by resolving flow along and perpendicular to AB.

steps.text: Take x along the flow (downstream) and y straight across the river. Since AB makes 45° with the straight-across direction, the flow direction makes 45° with AB.
steps.equation: angle between the flow velocity u and the line AB = 45°

steps.text: The man's resultant velocity relative to the ground must lie along AB. His velocity relative to water, v, satisfies v = v_resultant − u, so v is the vector from the tip of u to some point on the line AB.
Among all points on the line AB, the shortest vector from the tip of u to the line is the perpendicular distance from that point to the line, so the minimum |v| occurs when v is perpendicular to AB.
steps.why_this_step: The perpendicular distance from a point to a line through the origin at angle θ to the point's direction is (distance of point from origin) × sin θ.

final_answer.value: Minimum speed relative to water = u/√2, swum in the direction perpendicular to AB (tilted upstream), which makes 45° with the line perpendicular to the banks, tilted upstream.

common_mistakes.text: Swimming straight across (perpendicular to the bank) at speed u instead of perpendicular to AB gives a larger required speed and does not minimize |v|, since it ignores that AB is tilted from straight across.
